records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּשִׂ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And these [are] the judgments which you will set before them.
pieces: Here are the rules you are to lay before the people:

L.1: And these [are] the judgments that you will set before them:

decisions.choice: judgments: rulings for particular cases
decisions.reason: The word means a judge's decision, and so a binding ruling. Most of the rulings that follow are cases: "If someone does this, then this is to be done." Moses later tells the people "all the judgments", and they agree to keep them (24:3).

decisions.choice: these ... that you will set before them: the Book of the Covenant
decisions.reason: God is still speaking to Moses, as he has been since 20:22. The laws of 20:22-23:33 are called "the Book of the Covenant" when Moses reads them to the people (24:7). "Them" is Israel.

decisions.choice: rules (Balanced); laws (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "judgments", which can sound like verdicts against someone. Balanced says "rules", as in 24:3, and Readable "laws".

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people for "them".

records.heading: Hebrew slaves

records.source: כִּ֤י תִקְנֶה֙ עֶ֣בֶד עִבְרִ֔י שֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים יַעֲבֹ֑ד וּבַ֨שְּׁבִעִ֔ת יֵצֵ֥א לַֽחָפְשִׁ֖י חִנָּֽם׃
records.gloss: When you buy a Hebrew slave, six years he will serve, and in the seventh he will go out to freedom, for nothing.
pieces: When you acquire a Hebrew slave, he will serve six years; then in the seventh year he is to be released, free and owing nothing.

L.2: When you buy a Hebrew slave, six years he will serve, and in the seventh [year] he will go out free, for nothing.

R.2: Suppose you buy a Hebrew slave. He must work for you for six years. In the seventh year you must let him go free. He does not have to pay you anything.

decisions.choice: slave: a fellow Hebrew in debt servitude, limited to six years
decisions.reason: A Hebrew usually became a slave through debt or poverty, selling himself or being sold to pay what he owed (22:2; Leviticus 25:39; Deuteronomy 15:12). His service was limited to six years, and he went free in the seventh. This is not the chattel slavery of verses 20-21 and 32, where a slave is the owner's property ("his money", verse 21) and bound for life. The word is the ordinary word for a slave, a person owned and bound to work for another.

decisions.choice: Hebrew: a fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is the name used for Israelites in Exodus (1:15-16; 2:11; 3:18). Deuteronomy 15:12 says the same law applies to "your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman".

decisions.choice: go out free, for nothing: released without paying for his freedom
decisions.reason: "For nothing" means without a price. The slave owes nothing more when his six years end. Deuteronomy 15:13-14 adds that he is not to be sent away empty-handed.

decisions.choice: work for you
decisions.reason: Readable says "work" for "serve", which here means a slave's labor, not worship.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the Hebrew slave is bought and goes free in the seventh year (m1, m3).

records.source: אִם־בְּגַפּ֥וֹ יָבֹ֖א בְּגַפּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֑א אִם־בַּ֤עַל אִשָּׁה֙ ה֔וּא וְיָצְאָ֥ה אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: If with his body he comes, with his body he will go out; if he [is] husband of a wife, and will go out his wife with him.
pieces: If he arrived alone, he leaves alone. If he was married when he arrived, his wife leaves with him.

L.3: If he comes in by himself, by himself he will go out; if he [is] the husband of a wife, then his wife will go out with him.

R.3: If he was single when he came, he leaves alone. If he was married when he came, his wife goes free with him.

decisions.choice: with his body: by himself, without a wife
decisions.reason: The phrase means "his body alone", that is, unmarried. The second half of the verse supplies the contrast: a man who came with a wife.

decisions.choice: his wife will go out with him: the family he brought is not kept
decisions.reason: A wife who came into the service with her husband was not the master's property. When the husband's time ended, she left with him.

decisions.choice: single
decisions.reason: Readable says "single" and "married" for "by himself" and "husband of a wife".

records.source: אִם־אֲדֹנָיו֙ יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֔ה וְיָלְדָה־ל֥וֹ בָנִ֖ים א֣וֹ בָנ֑וֹת הָאִשָּׁ֣ה וִילָדֶ֗יהָ תִּהְיֶה֙ לַֽאדֹנֶ֔יהָ וְה֖וּא יֵצֵ֥א בְגַפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: If his master gives to him a wife and she bears to him sons or daughters, the wife and her children will belong to her master, and he will go out with his body.
pieces: If his master provides him with a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children remain the master's, and he goes out on his own.

L.4: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children will belong to her master, and he will go out by himself.

R.4: But suppose his master gave him a wife, and they had children. Then the wife and children still belong to the master. Only the man goes free.

decisions.choice: a wife given by the master: a woman who already belonged to the master
decisions.reason: The wife given to the slave was most likely the master's own slave woman, not bound by the six-year limit, so she and the children born to her stayed in the master's household. The text does not say where she came from.

decisions.choice: he will go out by himself: the hard choice of verses 5-6
decisions.reason: The slave may go free alone, or stay with his wife and children. The next two verses give the law for one who chooses to stay.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: Readable says "children" for "sons or daughters".

records.source: וְאִם־אָמֹ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אָהַ֨בְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֔י אֶת־אִשְׁתִּ֖י וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑י לֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א חָפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: And if surely says the slave, I love my master, my wife and my children; not I will go out free,
pieces: But suppose the slave says plainly, 'I love my master, my wife and my children. I will not leave as a free man.'

L.5: But if the slave plainly says, 'I love my master, my wife and my children; I will not go out free,'

R.5: But the slave may choose to stay. He may say, 'I love my master, and I love my wife and my children. I will not leave as a free man.'

decisions.choice: plainly says: declares clearly and on purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled, which stresses it. The slave's choice must be clear and openly stated, not forced from him.

decisions.choice: love: loyal attachment
decisions.reason: The slave loves his master's household as well as his own wife and children. Deuteronomy 15:16 gives the same case: he does not want to leave "because he loves you and your household, since he is well off with you".

decisions.choice: may choose to stay
decisions.reason: Readable first states the slave's choice in a short sentence, then gives his words.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the slave chooses not to go free (verse 2).

records.source: וְהִגִּישׁ֤וֹ אֲדֹנָיו֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהִגִּישׁוֹ֙ אֶל־הַדֶּ֔לֶת א֖וֹ אֶל־הַמְּזוּזָ֑ה וְרָצַ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤יו אֶת־אָזְנוֹ֙ בַּמַּרְצֵ֔עַ וַעֲבָד֖וֹ לְעֹלָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: then will bring him near his master to God, and he will bring him near to the door or to the doorpost, and will pierce his master his ear with an awl, and he will serve him forever.
pieces: his master shall bring him to God. Then he shall stand him by the door or the doorpost and drive an awl through his ear, and the man will serve him as a slave for life.

L.6: then his master will bring him near to God, and he will bring him near to the door or to the doorpost, and his master will pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve him forever.

R.6: Then his master must bring him to God. At the door or doorpost of the house, the master will push an awl, a sharp tool, through the slave's ear. Then the man will be his slave for life.

decisions.choice: to God: before God, perhaps at the place of worship
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for God. Here it may mean bringing the slave before God at a sanctuary, so that his choice is made before God. Or it may mean the judges, who decided cases in God's name, as the same word may in 22:7-8. Deuteronomy 15:17 mentions only the door of the house.

decisions.choice: the ear pierced at the door: a mark that the slave belongs to that house
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 15:17 says the awl goes through the ear "into the door", the door of the master's house. The ear is the organ of hearing and obeying, and the mark showed for all to see that the slave had joined that household for good.

decisions.choice: forever: for the rest of his life
decisions.reason: The phrase means for all time to come, here for as long as the slave lives (compare 1 Samuel 1:22).

decisions.choice: for life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "for life" for "forever"; Literal keeps "forever". Readable explains "awl" as a sharp tool.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the slave who refuses release belongs to the house for life (m2).

records.source: וְכִֽי־יִמְכֹּ֥ר אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאָמָ֑ה לֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א כְּצֵ֥את הָעֲבָדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And when sells a man his daughter as a female slave, not she will go out as the going out of the male slaves.
pieces: If a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she does not leave at the end of six years as the male slaves do.

L.7: And when a man sells his daughter as a slave woman, she will not go out as the male slaves go out.

R.7: Suppose a man sells his daughter as a maidservant. She does not go free after six years the way male slaves do.

decisions.choice: maidservant: a slave woman, here one taken as a wife or concubine
decisions.reason: The word means a female slave. Verses 8-10 show that this girl was bought to become the wife of her master or of his son, a wife of lower standing, often called a concubine. Her rights are those of a wife, not a laborer.

decisions.choice: she will not go out as the male slaves: she is protected by the rules of marriage
decisions.reason: She is not released after six years, because she has become part of the family by marriage. Instead verses 8-11 protect her from being sold, neglected or set aside. Deuteronomy 15:12 and 17 treat a woman sold for debt like a man.

decisions.choice: at the end of six years / after six years
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the release of verse 2 that "as the male slaves go out" refers to.

decisions.choice: male slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the daughter is sold, and the male slaves go free after six years (m2).

records.source: אִם־רָעָ֞ה בְּעֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־ל֥וֹ יְעָדָ֖הּ וְהֶפְדָּ֑הּ לְעַ֥ם נָכְרִ֛י לֹא־יִמְשֹׁ֥ל לְמָכְרָ֖הּ בְּבִגְדוֹ־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: If [she is] displeasing in the eyes of her master, who designated her for himself, then he will let her be redeemed; to a foreign people not he will have power to sell her, in his dealing treacherously with her.
pieces: Should her master, who had intended her for himself, find her displeasing, he must allow her to be redeemed. Since he has failed her, he may not sell her to people of another nation.

L.8: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, who designated her for himself, then he will let her be redeemed. To a foreign people he will have no power to sell her, since he has dealt faithlessly with her.

R.8: Her master may have planned to marry her and then is not pleased with her. If so, he must let her family buy her back. He has broken his promise to her, so he may not sell her to foreigners.

decisions.choice: for himself: the reading the Hebrew text marks to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a word that sounds the same and means "not", giving "who did not designate her", that is, he chose not to take her as wife. The scribes' note in the margin says to read "for himself": he had designated her for himself. The law is the same either way: he must not keep her and must not sell her abroad.

decisions.choice: let her be redeemed: allow her to be bought back
decisions.reason: The master must let her family, or someone else, pay to set her free. He may not keep her or resell her for profit.

decisions.choice: a foreign people; dealt faithlessly: he broke his commitment
decisions.reason: "Foreign people" means those outside Israel, and perhaps outside her own family and clan. Having failed to keep his commitment to her, the master loses the right to sell her anywhere she could not be redeemed.

decisions.choice: planned to marry her; her family buy her back
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "designated her for himself" means and who would redeem her. "Buy back" renders "redeem".

records.source: וְאִם־לִבְנ֖וֹ יִֽיעָדֶ֑נָּה כְּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הַבָּנ֖וֹת יַעֲשֶׂה־לָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And if for his son he designates her, according to the custom of the daughters he will do for her.
pieces: If he intends her for his son, he must deal with her as he would with a daughter of his own.

L.9: And if he designates her for his son, he will deal with her according to the custom for daughters.

R.9: If he gives her to his son to marry, he must treat her like his own daughter.

decisions.choice: the custom of daughters: the rights of a free daughter
decisions.reason: The word for "custom" is the same as "judgments" in verse 1. Given to the son as a wife, she is no longer treated as a slave but as a daughter of the house, with a daughter's rights and protection.

decisions.choice: to marry
decisions.reason: Readable states that "designates her for his son" means as the son's wife.

records.source: אִם־אַחֶ֖רֶת יִֽקַּֽח־ל֑וֹ שְׁאֵרָ֛הּ כְּסוּתָ֥הּ וְעֹנָתָ֖הּ לֹ֥א יִגְרָֽע׃
records.gloss: If another [woman] he takes for himself, her food, her covering and her marital rights not he will reduce.
pieces: Should he take a second wife, the first is still to have her full share of food, clothing and marital rights.

L.10: If he takes another [wife] for himself, her food, her clothing and her marital rights he will not reduce.

R.10: If he takes another wife, he must still give the first one all her food and clothes. He must also go on treating her as his wife.

decisions.choice: marital rights: her right to married life with her husband
decisions.reason: The third word occurs only here, and its meaning is uncertain. It most likely means the right to sexual relations in marriage (compare 1 Corinthians 7:3-5). Others take it as her lodging, or as oil for her body, a third basic need beside food and clothing.

decisions.choice: another wife: the first wife may not be neglected
decisions.reason: The law does not approve of taking two wives; it limits the harm done when it happens. The first wife keeps everything a wife is owed.

decisions.choice: the first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name "the first" wife, the girl of verses 7-9, so that "her" is clear.

records.source: וְאִם־שְׁלָ֨שׁ־אֵ֔לֶּה לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לָ֑הּ וְיָצְאָ֥ה חִנָּ֖ם אֵ֥ין כָּֽסֶף׃ס
records.gloss: And if these three not he does for her, she will go out for nothing; there is no money.
pieces: And if he fails her in these three things, she may leave free, with no price to pay.

L.11: And if he does not do these three [things] for her, she will go out for nothing, without money.

R.11: If he does not give her these three things, she may leave. She does not have to pay anything to go free.

decisions.choice: these three: food, clothing and marital rights
alternatives: redemption, marriage to the son, or full provision (verses 8-10)
decisions.reason: "These three" most likely refers back to the three things of verse 10. It may instead mean the three ways of treating her in verses 8-10: letting her be redeemed, giving her to his son as a daughter, or providing for her as a wife.

decisions.choice: she will go out for nothing: free, like the male slave of verse 2
decisions.reason: The same words "for nothing" are used of the male slave in verse 2. If her master fails her, she goes free without anyone paying for her.

records.source: מַכֵּ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ וָמֵ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: One striking a man and he dies, surely he will be put to death.
pieces: Whoever hits {{gender:another person|a man}} and kills {{gender:them|him}} must be put to death.

L.12: One who strikes {{gender:a person|a man}} so that {{gender:the person|he}} dies will surely be put to death.

R.12: If anyone strikes {{gender:someone|a man}} and {{gender:that person|he}} dies, the killer must be put to death.

decisions.choice: a man: any human being
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a man, used here of any person, man or woman (verse 28 names both). Taking a human life is the gravest crime because people are made in God's image (Genesis 9:6).

decisions.choice: surely be put to death: certainly be executed
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, a form used throughout these laws (verses 15-17). The penalty was carried out by the community after a trial with witnesses (Numbers 35:12, 30).

decisions.choice: {{gender:a person|a man}}
decisions.reason: Gender setting: the law covers every person, so the inclusive wording is the default and "a man" the alternative. The same applies wherever these laws speak of "a man" meaning anyone.

records.heading: Crimes deserving death

records.source: וַאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א צָדָ֔ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אִנָּ֣ה לְיָד֑וֹ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י לְךָ֙ מָק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנ֖וּס שָֽׁמָּה׃ס
records.gloss: And who did not lie in wait, but God let [it] happen to his hand, then I will appoint for you a place where he will flee there.
pieces: But if the killing was not planned, and God allowed it to happen, I will set aside a place for you where the killer can flee.

L.13: But [if] he did not lie in wait, but God let [it] happen to his hand, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.

R.13: But maybe the killer did not plan to do it, and it was an accident that God allowed. Then the killer may run to a safe place that I will choose for you.

decisions.choice: did not lie in wait: did not plan the killing
decisions.reason: To lie in wait is to plot and ambush. The killing was not intended.

decisions.choice: God let it happen to his hand: an accident
decisions.reason: The death came about without the killer's intent, though nothing happens outside God's rule. Deuteronomy 19:4-5 gives an example: an axe head flies off and kills a neighbor.

decisions.choice: a place where he may flee: the cities of refuge
decisions.reason: God later names six cities where one who killed by accident could find safety from the avenger until the case was judged (Numbers 35:9-28; Deuteronomy 19:1-13; Joshua 20).

decisions.choice: the killer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name "the killer" for "he", and Readable says "safe place".

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָזִ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ עַל־רֵעֵ֖הוּ לְהָרְג֣וֹ בְעָרְמָ֑ה מֵעִ֣ם מִזְבְּחִ֔י תִּקָּחֶ֖נּוּ לָמֽוּת׃ס
records.gloss: And when acts presumptuously a man against his neighbor to kill him with cunning, from with my altar you will take him to die.
pieces: But if {{gender:someone|a man}} schemes against {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and kills {{gender:them|him}} by treachery, take the killer away even from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar to be put to death.

L.14: And when {{gender:a person|a man}} acts presumptuously against {{gender:their|his}} neighbor to kill {{gender:them|him}} by cunning, from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar you will take [the killer] to die.

R.14: But if {{gender:someone|a man}} plans to kill another person and does it on purpose, you must put the killer to death. Take the killer away even from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, where people might run for safety.

decisions.choice: acts presumptuously ... with cunning: deliberate, planned murder
decisions.reason: The verb means to act boldly and willfully, and "cunning" means craft or trickery. This is the opposite of the accident in verse 13.

decisions.choice: from my altar you will take him: the altar is no refuge for a murderer
decisions.reason: One in danger might seize the altar to claim God's protection (1 Kings 1:50-53). This law denies that protection to a murderer, and Solomon acts on it with Joab (1 Kings 2:28-34).

decisions.choice: where people might run for safety
decisions.reason: Readable explains why a killer would be at the altar.

records.source: וּמַכֵּ֥ה אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And one striking his father and his mother, surely he will be put to death.
pieces: Whoever strikes father or mother must be put to death.

L.15: And one who strikes {{gender:their|his}} father or {{gender:their|his}} mother will surely be put to death.

R.15: Anyone who hits {{gender:their|his}} own father or mother must be put to death.

decisions.choice: strikes: attacks, even without killing
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 12, but here nothing is said of death. An attack on a parent, deadly or not, was a capital crime, because it overturned the honor owed to father and mother (20:12).

decisions.choice: father and mother: either parent
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his father and his mother", meaning either one, as verse 17 shows. Mother and father are protected alike.

records.source: וְגֹנֵ֨ב אִ֧ישׁ וּמְכָר֛וֹ וְנִמְצָ֥א בְיָד֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃ס
records.gloss: And one stealing a man and sells him, or he is found in his hand, surely he will be put to death.
pieces: Whoever steals {{gender:a person|a man}} must be put to death, and it makes no difference whether the captive has been sold or is found still held.

L.16: And one who steals {{gender:a person|a man}} and sells {{gender:them|him}}, or [the victim] is found in [the kidnapper's] hand, will surely be put to death.

R.16: Anyone who kidnaps {{gender:someone|a man}} must be put to death. It does not matter if the kidnapper has sold the victim or still has the victim.

decisions.choice: steals a man: kidnapping, usually to sell the victim as a slave
decisions.reason: To steal a person was to kidnap, as Joseph was "stolen" from his land and sold into Egypt (Genesis 37:28; 40:15). Deuteronomy 24:7 repeats the law for one who kidnaps a fellow Israelite. Paul names "enslavers" among the lawless (1 Timothy 1:10).

decisions.choice: and sells him, or he is found in his hand: in either case
decisions.reason: The crime deserves death whether the victim has already been sold or is still held by the kidnapper.

decisions.choice: kidnaps
decisions.reason: Readable says "kidnaps" for "steals a person".

records.source: וּמְקַלֵּ֥ל אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃ס
records.gloss: And one cursing his father and his mother, surely he will be put to death.
pieces: Whoever curses father or mother must be put to death.

L.17: And one who curses {{gender:their|his}} father or {{gender:their|his}} mother will surely be put to death.

R.17: Anyone who curses {{gender:their|his}} own father or mother must be put to death.

decisions.choice: curses: treats with contempt, calls down harm on
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the idea of being light, and means to treat someone as worthless or call evil on them. It is the reverse of honoring father and mother, a word that comes from the idea of weight (20:12). Leviticus 20:9 repeats the law, and Jesus quotes it in Matthew 15:4 and Mark 7:10.

L.20: And when {{gender:someone|a man}} strikes {{gender:their|his}} male slave or {{gender:their|his}} female slave with the rod, and [the slave] dies under {{gender:their|his}} hand, [the slave] will surely be avenged.

decisions.choice: surely be avenged: the slave's death must be punished
decisions.reason: The verb means to take vengeance, here by lawful punishment of the owner. A slave's life is protected by law like any other life. The penalty is not stated; it may be death, as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: dies under his hand: dies at once, while being beaten
decisions.reason: The slave dies during or right after the beating, so the owner's blows plainly caused the death.

decisions.choice: with the rod: discipline that turns deadly
decisions.reason: The rod was used for discipline (Proverbs 13:24). Even so, an owner who kills a slave with it is held to account.

decisions.choice: the owner must be punished
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who is punished for "he will be avenged".

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the ruling is about slaves owned as property (m1; verse 21).

records.source: אַ֥ךְ אִם־י֛וֹם א֥וֹ יוֹמַ֖יִם יַעֲמֹ֑ד לֹ֣א יֻקַּ֔ם כִּ֥י כַסְפּ֖וֹ הֽוּא׃ס

L.21: But if [the slave] survives a day or two days, [the slave] will not be avenged, for [the slave is] {{gender:their|his}} money.

R.21: But if the slave lives for a day or two before dying, the owner is not punished. The slave was the owner's own money, and the owner has lost it.

decisions.choice: survives a day or two: lives on at least a day or two

decisions.choice: before dying; the owner has lost it
decisions.reason: Readable states the reading taken and the reason behind "his money".

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the slave is the owner's money (m2).

records.gloss: And when struggle men and they strike a pregnant woman and come out her children, and there is not harm, surely he will be fined, as will impose on him the husband of the woman, and he will give by the assessments.
pieces: When men are fighting and they hit a pregnant woman so that her children are born early, but no further harm follows, the guilty man must pay a fine. The woman's husband sets the amount, and the payment is made as the judges determine.

L.22: And when men struggle together and strike a pregnant woman, and her children come out, but there is no harm, he will surely be fined, as the woman's husband lays on him, and he will give by the judges' [assessment].

decisions.choice: her children come out: a premature birth
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means that the child is born early but alive, so "no harm" means no further injury to mother or child. It may instead mean a miscarriage, with "no harm" referring to the mother alone. The plural "children" may simply mean whatever child or children she carries.

decisions.choice: harm: serious injury or death
decisions.reason: The word means disaster or fatal harm (Genesis 42:4, 38). Here it is not said whether the harm is to the mother, the child, or either one.

decisions.choice: by the judges: as the judges assess
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Deuteronomy 32:31; Job 31:11). It most likely means judges or an assessment, setting a limit on what the husband may demand.

decisions.choice: born early / comes out too soon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading in m1; the footnote gives the other. Readable says "baby".

R.24: an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot,

decisions.choice: eye for eye: the law of equivalence, which limits revenge
decisions.reason: The penalty is to be equal to the harm, and no greater. It sets a limit on revenge, the opposite of Lamech's boast to take vengeance seventy-sevenfold (Genesis 4:23-24). The same rule is given in Leviticus 24:19-20 and Deuteronomy 19:21. Jesus quotes it in Matthew 5:38-39 and tells his followers not to take even this measure of revenge.

decisions.choice: how it was applied: by judges, perhaps by payment
decisions.reason: The rule was for judges, not for private revenge. These same laws let a slave go free for an eye or a tooth (verses 26-27) and allow a ransom in place of a life (verse 30), and Numbers 35:31 forbids a ransom only for a murderer. So bodily harm may often have been settled by a payment equal to the loss.

decisions.choice: the ox will be stoned and not eaten: the animal answers for a human life
decisions.reason: God requires a reckoning for human blood, even from an animal (Genesis 9:5). The ox is put to death by stoning, and its meat may not be eaten, since it has taken a life.

decisions.choice: free: not guilty
decisions.reason: The owner had no reason to expect the ox to gore, so he bears no guilt. Verse 29 gives the case where he had been warned.

decisions.choice: ox: a head of cattle
decisions.reason: The word is used of a single bull, cow or ox, especially as a working animal.

records.heading: An ox that gores

records.source: וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ וְהֵמִ֥ית אִ֖ישׁ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה הַשּׁוֹר֙ יִסָּקֵ֔ל וְגַם־בְּעָלָ֖יו יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And if an ox prone to gore it [was] from yesterday [and] the third day, and it was warned to its owner, and not he guarded it, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox will be stoned, and also its owner will be put to death.
pieces: It is different if the ox was known to gore before. If its owner had been told of the danger and still failed to keep it in, and it then kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and the owner too must die.

L.29: But if the ox [was] prone to gore from yesterday [and] the third day, and its owner was warned, and he did not keep it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox will be stoned, and its owner also will be put to death.

R.29: But maybe the ox has attacked people with its horns before, and the owner was warned about it but did not keep it locked up. Then if it kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and the owner also deserves death.

decisions.choice: from yesterday and the third day: in the past
decisions.reason: The phrase means "before now", here in the time before this attack (compare 4:10; 5:7).

decisions.choice: its owner was warned and did not keep it in: guilt through negligence
decisions.reason: The owner knew the danger and did nothing, so he shares the guilt for the death. Verse 30 allows a ransom in his case, since he did not intend to kill.

decisions.choice: is laid on him: set by others

decisions.choice: thirty shekels of silver: about 12 ounces of silver
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight, not a coin; coins came much later. A shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce (11.5 grams), so thirty shekels was about 12 ounces of silver.

decisions.choice: thirty shekels: the price of a slave
decisions.reason: This sum, paid for a slave's life, became a byword for a low price. In Zechariah 11:12-13 the shepherd is paid thirty pieces of silver, and the priests pay Judas the same to betray Jesus (Matthew 26:15; 27:9-10).

decisions.choice: to his master: the slave as property
decisions.reason: The payment goes to the slave's master for his loss, as for a chattel slave (verse 21). The ox is still stoned, since it has taken a human life.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 12 ounces of silver|30 shekels of silver}}
decisions.reason: Units setting: the modern weight by default, "30 shekels of silver" as the alternative. Literal keeps the shekels. Readable says "kills" for "gores", as the ruling of verses 28-29 is about a death.

decisions.choice: opens or digs and does not cover: careless with a danger
decisions.reason: Whether the pit is old and reopened or newly dug, the one who leaves it open is responsible for what falls in.

records.heading: Paying for a neighbor's loss

records.source: בַּ֤עַל הַבּוֹר֙ יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם כֶּ֖סֶף יָשִׁ֣יב לִבְעָלָ֑יו וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: the owner of the pit will make good; silver he will return to its owner, and the dead will belong to him.
pieces: The pit's owner must make good the loss by paying the animal's owner in silver, and may keep the dead animal.

L.34: the owner of the pit will make restitution; silver {{gender:they|he}} will pay back to its owner, and the dead [animal] will be {{gender:theirs|his}}.

R.34: The owner of the pit must pay the animal's owner for it with money. Then the dead animal belongs to the one who paid.

decisions.choice: make restitution: make good the loss in full
decisions.reason: The verb means to make whole, to pay back what was lost. It is used throughout these laws (verses 36-37; 22:2-14).

decisions.choice: the dead will be his: the carcass offsets the payment
decisions.reason: The one who paid keeps the dead animal, whose hide and meat were worth something.

records.source: וְכִֽי־יִגֹּ֧ף שֽׁוֹר־אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־שׁ֥וֹר רֵעֵ֖הוּ וָמֵ֑ת וּמָ֨כְר֜וּ אֶת־הַשּׁ֤וֹר הַחַי֙ וְחָצ֣וּ אֶת־כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַמֵּ֖ת יֶֽחֱצֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And when strikes the ox of a man the ox of his neighbor and it dies, they will sell the living ox and divide its silver, and also the dead they will divide.
pieces: If {{gender:someone's|a man's}} ox injures {{gender:their|his}} neighbor's ox and it dies, they are to sell the ox that is alive and share the price, and share the dead one too.

L.35: And when {{gender:someone's|a man's}} ox strikes the ox of {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and it dies, they will sell the living ox and divide its silver, and they will also divide the dead [animal].

R.35: If {{gender:someone's|a man's}} ox hurts another person's ox and it dies, the two owners must sell the living ox and split the money. They must also split the dead ox.

decisions.choice: they will divide: the loss is shared equally
decisions.reason: Neither owner was at fault, so the two share the loss: each gets half the price of the living ox and half of the dead one.

decisions.choice: strikes: butts or gores
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or push, here with the horns.

records.source: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו שַׁלֵּ֨ם יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שׁוֹר֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: Or it is known that an ox prone to gore it [was] from yesterday [and] the third day, and not guarded it its owner, surely he will make good ox in place of the ox, and the dead will belong to him.
pieces: But if people knew the ox had a habit of goring and its owner still left it loose, that owner must replace the dead ox with a live one, and the dead one becomes the owner's.

L.36: Or [if] it is known that the ox [was] prone to gore from yesterday [and] the third day, and its owner has not kept it in, {{gender:they|he}} will surely make restitution, ox for ox, and the dead [animal] will be {{gender:theirs|his}}.

R.36: But if everyone knew the ox had attacked before and the owner did not keep it locked up, the owner must give a living ox to replace the dead one. Then the owner may keep the dead ox.

decisions.choice: known to gore and not kept in: the careless owner bears the whole loss
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, the owner knew the danger. He must pay a whole ox for the one killed, keeping the dead animal.

records.source: כִּ֤י יִגְנֹֽב־אִישׁ֙ שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֔ה וּטְבָח֖וֹ א֣וֹ מְכָר֑וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בָקָ֗ר יְשַׁלֵּם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְאַרְבַּע־צֹ֖אן תַּ֥חַת הַשֶּֽׂה׃
records.gloss: When steals a man an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, five cattle he will repay in place of the ox, and four sheep in place of the sheep.
pieces: If {{gender:someone|a man}} steals an ox or a sheep and butchers it or sells it, the thief must replace the ox with five cattle and the sheep with four sheep.

L.37: When {{gender:someone|a man}} steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, five cattle {{gender:they|he}} will repay for the ox, and four sheep for the sheep.

R.37: If {{gender:someone|a man}} steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, the thief must give back five cattle for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 21:37 is 22:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does, where chapter 21 has 37 verses. Many Bibles begin chapter 22 with this verse, so 21:37 here is 22:1 there, and 22:1-30 here is 22:2-31 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: five for an ox, four for a sheep: repayment many times over
decisions.reason: A thief who has already killed or sold the animal pays it back many times over; if it is found alive, he pays double (22:3). The ox, a working animal, costs more. David's verdict on the rich man (2 Samuel 12:6) and Zacchaeus's promise (Luke 19:8) both speak of paying back fourfold.

decisions.choice: sheep: one animal of the flock
decisions.reason: The first word means a single sheep or goat; the second, the flock. Both may include goats.
